Class UtcToPacificTimestamps

java.lang.Object
edu.ucsb.cs.taapply.migration.UtcToPacificTimestamps
All Implemented Interfaces:
liquibase.change.custom.CustomChange, liquibase.change.custom.CustomTaskChange, liquibase.change.custom.CustomTaskRollback
public class UtcToPacificTimestamps extends Object implements liquibase.change.custom.CustomTaskChange, liquibase.change.custom.CustomTaskRollback
The one-time conversion of issue #293: every zone-less TIMESTAMP column the app wrote with LocalDateTime.now() or a Hibernate timestamp generator while the server ran in UTC holds UTC wall-clock time; this rewrites each value as the Pacific wall-clock time of the same instant. From then on the app writes Pacific wall-clock time (AppTime), so the column means one thing throughout.

Rolling the change back converts every value from Pacific back to UTC. The forward direction loses nothing. The backward direction cannot tell the two passes through the hour that repeats when clocks fall back each November (1:00 to 1:59 a.m. occurs twice); it takes the first, so a value stamped in the second pass comes back an hour early. A value in the hour skipped when clocks spring forward cannot occur.

The columns that hold an exact instant (users.last_online, a TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE) and the quarter calendar copied from the UCSB API (already Pacific) are left alone. Tables or columns that do not exist yet (a fresh database, or the lib-jobs tables that a later changelog creates) are skipped.
